```{python}
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from zipfile import ZipFile
import json
import shutil

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import tensorflow as tf
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, classification_report, confusion_matrix, f1_score
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from tensorflow.keras import callbacks, layers, models, optimizers
from tensorflow.keras.utils import to_categorical

SEED = 42
IMAGE_SIZE = (32, 32)
BATCH_SIZE = 64
EPOCHS = 30
DARK_LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD = 0.20
tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(SEED)

# Support running from either MachineLearning or its notebooks folder.
NOTEBOOK_DIR = next(
    (folder for folder in (Path.cwd(), Path.cwd() / "notebooks")
     if all((folder / name).is_file()
            for name in ("training1.zip", "training2.zip"))),
    None,
)
if NOTEBOOK_DIR is None:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Place training1.zip and training2.zip beside module5_signs.qmd, "
        "then run from the MachineLearning or notebooks folder."
    )

DATA_DIR = NOTEBOOK_DIR / "cnn_training_data"
BASELINE_DIR = NOTEBOOK_DIR / "cnn_training_output"
PREVIOUS_MODEL_DIR = BASELINE_DIR / "improved"
OUTPUT_DIR = BASELINE_DIR / "lighting_enhanced"
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

## Extract and combine both archives

Each image's parent folder supplies its class label. We preserve the archive
folders so identical filenames in different classes cannot overwrite each other.
Existing extracted images with the expected size are reused on subsequent runs.
Only files listed in the two archives enter the dataset.

```{python}
records = []
for archive_name in ("training1.zip", "training2.zip"):
    with ZipFile(NOTEBOOK_DIR / archive_name) as archive:
        for member in archive.infolist():
            if member.is_dir():
                continue
            relative = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
            if (
                len(relative.parts) != 3
                or relative.parts[0] != Path(archive_name).stem
                or not relative.parts[1].isdigit()
                or relative.suffix.lower() != ".jpg"
                or "\\" in member.filename
                or ".." in relative.parts
            ):
                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected archive entry: {member.filename}")

            destination = DATA_DIR.joinpath(*relative.parts)
            destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            if (not destination.is_file()
                    or destination.stat().st_size != member.file_size):
                with archive.open(member) as source, destination.open("wb") as target:
                    shutil.copyfileobj(source, target)

            # Treat a shared filename prefix as one related-image sequence.
            sequence = relative.stem.split("_")[0]
            records.append({
                "path": str(destination.resolve()),
                "class_name": relative.parts[1],
                "group": f"{relative.parts[0]}/{relative.parts[1]}/{sequence}",
            })

images = pd.DataFrame(records).sort_values("path").reset_index(drop=True)
class_names = sorted(images["class_name"].unique().tolist())
class_to_index = {name: index for index, name in enumerate(class_names)}
images["label"] = images["class_name"].map(class_to_index)
NUM_CLASSES = len(class_names)
print(f"Loaded {len(images):,} image paths across {NUM_CLASSES} classes.")
images.groupby("class_name").size().rename("image_count").to_frame()
```

## Create training, validation, and test sets

Use approximately 70% of filename sequences for training, 15% for validation,
and 15% for testing, stratified by class. Filenames such as `00043_00015.jpg`
suggest a sequence prefix (`00043`) and an image number (`00015`). We assume
images with the same prefix in the same class and archive are related and keep
them together to reduce leakage. Exact image percentages can vary because
sequences can have different lengths. These are internal holdouts from the
provided archives, not a separate official test dataset.

```{python}
groups = images[["group", "label"]].drop_duplicates()
train_groups, holdout_groups = train_test_split(
    groups, test_size=0.30, stratify=groups["label"], random_state=SEED
)
validation_groups, test_groups = train_test_split(
    holdout_groups, test_size=0.50,
    stratify=holdout_groups["label"], random_state=SEED
)

def select_images(selected_groups):
    return images[images["group"].isin(selected_groups["group"])].reset_index(drop=True)

train_images = select_images(train_groups)
validation_images = select_images(validation_groups)
test_images = select_images(test_groups)

assert set(train_images["group"]).isdisjoint(validation_images["group"])
assert set(train_images["group"]).isdisjoint(test_images["group"])
assert set(validation_images["group"]).isdisjoint(test_images["group"])
assert len(train_images) + len(validation_images) + len(test_images) == len(images)
for frame in (train_images, validation_images, test_images):
    assert set(frame["label"]) == set(range(NUM_CLASSES))

pd.DataFrame({
    "split": ["Training", "Validation", "Test"],
    "images": [len(train_images), len(validation_images), len(test_images)],
    "sequences": [len(train_groups), len(validation_groups), len(test_groups)],
})
```

## Preprocessing and lighting improvements

**Johnny, Data Science Intern:**

The training and test images have three color channels, (Red, Green, and Blue), with pixel values for each channel ranging from 0 to 255.

Do you think we need to do any preprocessing before using the data to train the model?

The image preprocessing and lighting helpers are grouped here. Choose the lighting recipe using validation predictions after training.

### Resize, normalize, and encode labels

Like the guide, scale pixels to the range 0–1 and one-hot encode labels for
categorical cross-entropy. Load images in batches using `tf.data` instead of
holding all decoded images in memory. Only the training dataset is shuffled;
test predictions must stay aligned with the test labels.

```{python}
def load_image(path, label):
    image = tf.io.decode_jpeg(tf.io.read_file(path), channels=3)
    image = tf.image.resize(image, IMAGE_SIZE)
    image = tf.cast(image, tf.float32) / 255.0
    return image, label

def preprocess_holdout(image_bytes):
    image = tf.io.decode_jpeg(image_bytes, channels=3)
    image = tf.image.resize(image, IMAGE_SIZE)
    return tf.cast(image, tf.float32) / 255.0

def make_dataset(frame, training=False):
    labels = to_categorical(frame["label"].to_numpy(), num_classes=NUM_CLASSES)
    dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((frame["path"].to_numpy(), labels))
    if training:
        dataset = dataset.shuffle(len(frame), seed=SEED)
    dataset = dataset.map(load_image, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
    return dataset.batch(BATCH_SIZE).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

train_ds = make_dataset(train_images, training=True)
validation_ds = make_dataset(validation_images)
test_ds = make_dataset(test_images)

sample_images, sample_labels = next(iter(train_ds))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(10, 5))
for index, axis in enumerate(axes.flat):
    axis.imshow(sample_images[index].numpy())
    axis.set_title(f"Class {class_names[int(tf.argmax(sample_labels[index]))]}")
    axis.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Improve lighting for dark images

Some signs are very dark. Compare predictions on original images, gamma-adjusted
copies, and copies with stronger contrast. Gamma below 1 brightens normalized
pixels, as described in the [TensorFlow gamma-correction documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/image/adjust_gamma).
Contrast enhancement maps each color channel's 1st to 99th percentile into
the range 0–1, clipping extreme values. A constant channel keeps its original
values. This can reveal faint symbols, but also amplify noise or change colors.
It cannot restore detail lost to blur, clipping, or very low resolution.

For this experiment, a dark image has mean luminance below 0.20 on a 0–1 scale.
The threshold is a diagnostic definition, not a guarantee of image quality.

```{python}
def mean_luminance(images):
    return tf.reduce_mean(tf.image.rgb_to_grayscale(images), axis=(-3, -2, -1))

def stretch_contrast(images):
    """Stretch the 1st–99th percentiles of each RGB channel; accept HWC or NHWC."""
    images = tf.convert_to_tensor(images, dtype=tf.float32)
    unbatched = images.shape.rank == 3
    batch = images[tf.newaxis, ...] if unbatched else images
    flat = tf.reshape(batch, (tf.shape(batch)[0], -1, 3))
    ordered = tf.sort(flat, axis=1)
    pixels = tf.shape(flat)[1]
    low_index = tf.cast(0.01 * tf.cast(pixels - 1, tf.float32), tf.int32)
    high_index = tf.cast(0.99 * tf.cast(pixels - 1, tf.float32), tf.int32)
    low = tf.gather(ordered, low_index, axis=1)[:, tf.newaxis, tf.newaxis, :]
    high = tf.gather(ordered, high_index, axis=1)[:, tf.newaxis, tf.newaxis, :]
    span = high - low
    adjusted = tf.clip_by_value((batch - low) / tf.maximum(span, 1e-6), 0, 1)
    adjusted = tf.where(span > 1e-6, adjusted, batch)
    return adjusted[0] if unbatched else adjusted

def adjust_lighting(images, variant):
    if variant in ("dark_contrast", "dark_contrast_gamma_0.7"):
        adjusted = stretch_contrast(images)
        if variant == "dark_contrast_gamma_0.7":
            adjusted = tf.image.adjust_gamma(adjusted, gamma=0.7)
        dark = mean_luminance(images) < DARK_LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD
        return tf.where(
            dark[..., tf.newaxis, tf.newaxis, tf.newaxis],
            adjusted, tf.image.adjust_gamma(images, gamma=0.5),
        )
    if variant == "contrast":
        return stretch_contrast(images)
    if variant == "contrast_gamma_0.7":
        return tf.image.adjust_gamma(stretch_contrast(images), gamma=0.7)
    return tf.image.adjust_gamma(images, gamma=float(variant))

def predict_with_lighting(cnn, inputs, variants=(1.0,)):
    """Average class probabilities over the chosen lighting variations."""
    if not variants:
        raise ValueError("At least one lighting variant is required.")
    if isinstance(inputs, tf.data.Dataset) and isinstance(inputs.element_spec, tuple):
        image_inputs = inputs.map(lambda images, labels: images)
    else:
        image_inputs = inputs
    predictions = []
    for variant in variants:
        if isinstance(image_inputs, tf.data.Dataset):
            adjusted_inputs = image_inputs
            if variant != 1.0:
                adjusted_inputs = image_inputs.map(
                    lambda images: adjust_lighting(images, variant),
                    num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE,
                )
        else:
            adjusted_inputs = adjust_lighting(image_inputs, variant)
        predictions.append(cnn.predict(adjusted_inputs, verbose=0))
    return np.mean(predictions, axis=0)
```

## Data augmentation

**Emma, CEO of GehirnWagen:**

I'm concerned that the model will only be able to recognize signs that look exactly like the ones we have images for.

I understand from Johnny that data augmentation can help with this problem. What strategy would you suggest?

Small rotations, translations, zoom changes, and contrast changes create
additional training variations. Do not flip traffic signs: a mirrored sign can
have a different meaning. Keras applies these augmentation layers during
training and disables them during prediction.
These follow the techniques
in the [TensorFlow image-classification tutorial](https://www.tensorflow.org/tutorials/images/classification).

```{python}
data_augmentation = models.Sequential([
    layers.RandomRotation(0.025, seed=SEED),
    layers.RandomTranslation(0.05, 0.05, seed=SEED + 1),
    layers.RandomZoom(0.10, seed=SEED + 2),
    layers.RandomContrast(0.15, value_range=(0, 1), seed=SEED + 3),
], name="training_augmentation")
```

## Train a CNN that handles more variation

Use the augmentation pipeline as the first model stage. Dropout helps reduce overfitting.

Class weights are computed using training labels only. They give images from
smaller classes more influence on the training loss. Validation and test sets
keep their original class distributions. Early stopping restores the weights
with the lowest validation loss, and the learning rate decreases when that loss
stalls. If the earlier saved model has matching class labels and weight shapes,
reuse its learned weights and fine-tune at a lower learning rate. Otherwise,
train from scratch. Increasing the epoch limit alone does not guarantee better
predictions.

```{python}
model = models.Sequential([
    layers.Input(shape=(*IMAGE_SIZE, 3)),
    data_augmentation,
    layers.Conv2D(32, (3, 3), activation="relu"),
    layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
    layers.Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation="relu"),
    layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
    layers.Flatten(),
    layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"),
    layers.Dropout(0.20),
    layers.Dense(NUM_CLASSES, activation="softmax"),
])

starting_learning_rate = 0.001
initial_model_path = BASELINE_DIR / "cnn_sign_model.keras"
initial_labels_path = BASELINE_DIR / "class_names.json"
if initial_model_path.is_file() and initial_labels_path.is_file():
    initial_class_names = json.loads(initial_labels_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    initial_model = models.load_model(initial_model_path, compile=False)
    initial_weights = initial_model.get_weights()
    expected_weights = model.get_weights()
    weights_match = (
        len(initial_weights) == len(expected_weights)
        and all(old.shape == new.shape
                for old, new in zip(initial_weights, expected_weights))
    )
    if initial_class_names == class_names and weights_match:
        model.set_weights(initial_weights)
        starting_learning_rate = 0.0001
        print("Fine-tuning the earlier saved CNN with learning rate 0.0001.")
    else:
        print("Earlier model is incompatible; training from scratch.")
else:
    print("No earlier saved CNN found; training from scratch.")

model.compile(
    optimizer=optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=starting_learning_rate),
    loss="categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"],
)
model.summary()

training_class_counts = train_images["label"].value_counts()
class_weights = {
    int(label): float(len(train_images) / (NUM_CLASSES * count))
    for label, count in training_class_counts.items()
}
training_callbacks = [
    callbacks.EarlyStopping(
        monitor="val_loss", patience=8, restore_best_weights=True, verbose=1,
    ),
    callbacks.ReduceLROnPlateau(
        monitor="val_loss", factor=0.5, patience=3, min_lr=1e-5, verbose=1,
    ),
    callbacks.CSVLogger(str(OUTPUT_DIR / "training_history.csv")),
]
history = model.fit(
    train_ds,
    epochs=EPOCHS,
    validation_data=validation_ds,
    class_weight=class_weights,
    callbacks=training_callbacks,
    shuffle=False,  # train_ds already shuffles the image paths.
    verbose=2,
)
```

## Check whether the weaker classes improve

Compare models on the same labeled validation images. Macro F1 gives each
class equal importance, so a large class cannot hide weak performance on a
small class. The per-class table below is sorted by recall, showing the classes
whose images are missed most often. Use these validation results to choose
changes; evaluate the selected model on the internal test set afterward.
The unlabeled holdout archive cannot measure accuracy.

Apply the new contrast correction only to dark images. Brighter images retain
the previous original-plus-gamma-0.5 average. This avoids changing their input
contrast unnecessarily. Select the recipe with the highest dark-image validation
accuracy, provided its overall validation accuracy and macro F1 are at least as
good as the previous recipe. Break ties with overall macro F1 and accuracy.
Thus brighter-looking images or higher prediction probabilities alone cannot
justify replacing the previous recipe. The selected recipe is used consistently
on test and holdout images; a two-image average costs two prediction passes.
Manually reviewed holdout examples are not used to choose the recipe.

```{python}
validation_true = validation_images["label"].to_numpy()

validation_luminance = np.concatenate([
    mean_luminance(batch).numpy() for batch, labels in validation_ds
])
validation_dark = validation_luminance < DARK_LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD
print(f"Dark validation images: {validation_dark.sum():,} / {len(validation_dark):,}")

def validation_metrics(name, predicted):
    return {
        "model": name,
        "validation_accuracy": accuracy_score(validation_true, predicted),
        "validation_macro_f1": f1_score(
            validation_true, predicted, labels=np.arange(NUM_CLASSES),
            average="macro", zero_division=0,
        ),
        "dark_validation_accuracy": (
            accuracy_score(validation_true[validation_dark], predicted[validation_dark])
            if validation_dark.any() else np.nan
        ),
    }

# Compute each lighting variation once, then compare inexpensive averages.
validation_by_variant = {
    variant: predict_with_lighting(model, validation_ds, variants=(variant,))
    for variant in (1.0, 0.5, 0.7, "contrast", "contrast_gamma_0.7")
}
# These are image-wise switches, not averages of two transformations.
# Reuse cached probabilities to avoid two more full validation passes.
for targeted, enhanced in (("dark_contrast", "contrast"),
                          ("dark_contrast_gamma_0.7", "contrast_gamma_0.7")):
    validation_by_variant[targeted] = np.where(
        validation_dark[:, np.newaxis],
        validation_by_variant[enhanced], validation_by_variant[0.5],
    )
lighting_recipes = {
    "Original": (1.0,),
    "Gamma 0.5": (0.5,),
    "Gamma 0.7": (0.7,),
    "Original + gamma 0.5": (1.0, 0.5),
    "Original + gamma 0.7": (1.0, 0.7),
    "Original + gamma 0.5 + gamma 0.7": (1.0, 0.5, 0.7),
    "Contrast only": ("contrast",),
    "Contrast + gamma 0.7 only": ("contrast_gamma_0.7",),
    "Original + contrast": (1.0, "contrast"),
    "Original + contrast + gamma 0.7": (1.0, "contrast_gamma_0.7"),
    "Original + contrast (dark only)": (1.0, "dark_contrast"),
    "Original + contrast + gamma 0.7 (dark only)": (1.0, "dark_contrast_gamma_0.7"),
}
lighting_rows = []
for name, variants in lighting_recipes.items():
    combined = np.mean([validation_by_variant[variant] for variant in variants], axis=0)
    lighting_rows.append(validation_metrics(name, combined.argmax(axis=1)))
lighting_comparison = pd.DataFrame(lighting_rows)
previous_lighting = lighting_comparison[
    lighting_comparison["model"] == "Original + gamma 0.5"
].iloc[0]
lighting_comparison["eligible_for_selection"] = (
    (lighting_comparison["validation_accuracy"] >= previous_lighting["validation_accuracy"])
    & (lighting_comparison["validation_macro_f1"] >= previous_lighting["validation_macro_f1"])
)
# Full-image contrast variants stay in the diagnostic table, but only targeted
# corrections or the previous recipe can become the final prediction method.
lighting_comparison["eligible_for_selection"] &= lighting_comparison["model"].isin([
    "Original + gamma 0.5",
    "Original + contrast (dark only)",
    "Original + contrast + gamma 0.7 (dark only)",
])
if validation_dark.any():
    lighting_comparison["eligible_for_selection"] &= (
        lighting_comparison["dark_validation_accuracy"]
        >= previous_lighting["dark_validation_accuracy"]
    )
selection_columns = (
    ["dark_validation_accuracy", "validation_macro_f1", "validation_accuracy"]
    if validation_dark.any() else ["validation_macro_f1", "validation_accuracy"]
)
lighting_comparison = lighting_comparison.sort_values(selection_columns, ascending=False)
lighting_comparison.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "lighting_comparison.csv", index=False)
selected_recipe = lighting_comparison[
    lighting_comparison["eligible_for_selection"]
].iloc[0]["model"]
inference_variants = lighting_recipes[selected_recipe]
print(f"Selected lighting recipe: {selected_recipe}")
print(lighting_comparison.to_string(index=False))
validation_probabilities = np.mean(
    [validation_by_variant[variant] for variant in inference_variants], axis=0,
)
validation_predicted = validation_probabilities.argmax(axis=1)

comparison_rows = []
baseline_class_recalls = None
baseline_path = BASELINE_DIR / "cnn_sign_model.keras"
baseline_labels_path = BASELINE_DIR / "class_names.json"
if baseline_path.is_file() and baseline_labels_path.is_file():
    baseline_class_names = json.loads(baseline_labels_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if baseline_class_names == class_names:
        baseline_model = models.load_model(baseline_path, compile=False)
        baseline_predicted = baseline_model.predict(validation_ds, verbose=0).argmax(axis=1)
        comparison_rows.append(validation_metrics("Previous saved CNN", baseline_predicted))
        baseline_class_recalls = np.diag(confusion_matrix(
            validation_true, baseline_predicted,
            labels=np.arange(NUM_CLASSES), normalize="true",
        ))
    else:
        print("Previous model has a different class order; comparison skipped.")
comparison_rows.append(validation_metrics("Augmented, regularized CNN", validation_predicted))
comparison_rows.append(previous_lighting.to_dict())
validation_comparison = pd.DataFrame(comparison_rows)
validation_comparison.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "validation_comparison.csv", index=False)
print(validation_comparison.to_string(index=False))

validation_report = classification_report(
    validation_true, validation_predicted, labels=np.arange(NUM_CLASSES),
    target_names=class_names, output_dict=True, zero_division=0,
)
validation_class_report = pd.DataFrame(validation_report).T.loc[class_names]
if baseline_class_recalls is not None:
    validation_class_report["previous_recall"] = pd.Series(
        baseline_class_recalls, index=class_names,
    )
    validation_class_report["recall_change"] = (
        validation_class_report["recall"] - validation_class_report["previous_recall"]
    )
validation_class_report = validation_class_report.sort_values("recall")
validation_class_report.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "validation_class_report.csv", index_label="class")
validation_class_report
```

### Inspect confidently wrong validation predictions

These labeled examples show actual mistakes, including mistakes made with high
model probabilities. Review recurring patterns such as blur, lighting, framing,
or very similar symbols before changing the augmentation settings. A model
probability is a prediction score, not measured accuracy.

```{python}
validation_errors = validation_images.copy()
validation_errors["predicted_label"] = validation_predicted
validation_errors["model_probability"] = validation_probabilities.max(axis=1)
validation_errors = validation_errors[
    validation_errors["label"] != validation_errors["predicted_label"]
].sort_values("model_probability", ascending=False)
validation_errors.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "validation_errors.csv", index=False)

if validation_errors.empty:
    print("No misclassified validation images.")
else:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(11, 7))
    for axis, (_, example) in zip(axes.flat, validation_errors.head(6).iterrows()):
        image, _ = load_image(example["path"], 0)
        axis.imshow(image.numpy())
        axis.set_title(
            f"Actual {example['class_name']}\n"
            f"Predicted {class_names[int(example['predicted_label'])]} "
            f"(p={example['model_probability']:.2f})"
        )
    for axis in axes.flat:
        axis.axis("off")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

## Review the learning curves

Compare training and validation results when adjusting the model. A growing gap
can indicate overfitting. These curves describe the base CNN; the validation
table above reports the selected lighting recipe. Reserve the test set for
evaluating the final model.

```{python}
epochs = range(1, len(history.history["loss"]) + 1)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))
for axis, metric, title in zip(axes, ("accuracy", "loss"), ("Accuracy", "Loss")):
    axis.plot(epochs, history.history[metric], label="Training")
    axis.plot(epochs, history.history[f"val_{metric}"], label="Validation")
    axis.set(xlabel="Epoch", ylabel=title, title=f"Training and validation {metric}")
    axis.set_xticks(list(epochs))
    axis.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Model evaluation

**Johnny, Data Science Intern:**

This seems like one of those cases where straight accuracy might not be the best metric for model evaluation, but what do you think?

### Evaluate held-out images and draw the confusion matrix

The guide's prediction and confusion-matrix workflow now uses the internal test
set from both archives. Report per-class precision, recall, and F1 because the
class sizes differ. Folder IDs are used as labels; the archives do not include
a file mapping IDs to readable class names.

We have inspected this test set during iterative development, so these
comparisons are diagnostic. Use fresh labeled images for a final unbiased
assessment of the completed model and preprocessing choices.

```{python}
y_true = test_images["label"].to_numpy()
test_probabilities = predict_with_lighting(model, test_ds, inference_variants)
y_pred = test_probabilities.argmax(axis=1)
test_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
test_loss = float(np.mean(tf.keras.losses.categorical_crossentropy(
    to_categorical(y_true, num_classes=NUM_CLASSES), test_probabilities,
)))
print(f"Test loss: {test_loss:.4f}")
print(f"Test accuracy: {test_accuracy:.2%}")
test_luminance = np.concatenate([mean_luminance(batch).numpy() for batch, labels in test_ds])
test_dark = test_luminance < DARK_LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD
if test_dark.any():
    print(f"Dark-image test accuracy: {accuracy_score(y_true[test_dark], y_pred[test_dark]):.2%}")

# Report the old and selected lighting methods on this same final test set.
previous_test_predicted = predict_with_lighting(model, test_ds, (1.0, 0.5)).argmax(axis=1)
test_comparison_rows = []
for name, predicted in (("Previous lighting", previous_test_predicted),
                        (selected_recipe, y_pred)):
    test_comparison_rows.append({
        "recipe": name,
        "test_accuracy": accuracy_score(y_true, predicted),
        "test_macro_f1": f1_score(y_true, predicted, average="macro", zero_division=0),
        "dark_test_accuracy": (
            accuracy_score(y_true[test_dark], predicted[test_dark])
            if test_dark.any() else np.nan
        ),
        "dark_test_images": int(test_dark.sum()),
    })
test_lighting_comparison = pd.DataFrame(test_comparison_rows)
test_lighting_comparison.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "test_lighting_comparison.csv", index=False)
print(test_lighting_comparison.to_string(index=False))

print(classification_report(
    y_true, y_pred, labels=np.arange(NUM_CLASSES),
    target_names=class_names, zero_division=0,
))

cm = confusion_matrix(
    y_true,
    y_pred,
    labels=np.arange(NUM_CLASSES),
    normalize="true",
)

plt.figure(figsize=(13, 11))
sns.heatmap(
    cm,
    cmap="Blues",
    vmin=0,
    vmax=1,
    xticklabels=class_names,
    yticklabels=class_names,
    cbar_kws={"label": "Fraction of images in the true class"},
)
plt.xlabel("Predicted class")
plt.ylabel("Actual class")
plt.title("Classification results by class")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Save and reload the model

Save in the Keras format along with the ordered class labels and selected
lighting recipe. New images must use the same RGB conversion, resizing, and
0–1 normalization as the training images. Use `predict_with_lighting` with the
saved recipe to reproduce the final predictions; calling the Keras model alone
gives the base CNN predictions. Re-running this section replaces the previous
lighting-enhanced artifacts in `cnn_training_output/lighting_enhanced`.

```{python}
model_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "cnn_sign_model.keras"
labels_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "class_names.json"
inference_config_path = OUTPUT_DIR / "inference_config.json"
model.save(model_path)
labels_path.write_text(json.dumps(class_names, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
inference_config_path.write_text(
    json.dumps({
        "variants": list(inference_variants),
        "contrast_percentiles": [1, 99],
        "dark_luminance_threshold": DARK_LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD,
    }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8",
)

loaded_model = models.load_model(model_path)
loaded_class_names = json.loads(labels_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
loaded_inference_config = json.loads(
    inference_config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
)
# Also accept the earlier gamma-only configuration format.
loaded_inference_variants = loaded_inference_config.get(
    "variants", loaded_inference_config.get("gammas", [1.0])
)
example_image, _ = load_image(test_images.iloc[0]["path"], 0)
probabilities = predict_with_lighting(
    loaded_model, example_image[tf.newaxis, ...], loaded_inference_variants,
)[0]
predicted_class = loaded_class_names[int(np.argmax(probabilities))]
print(f"Saved model: {model_path}")
print(f"Example actual class: {test_images.iloc[0]['class_name']}")
print(f"Example predicted class: {predicted_class}")
```

## Predict the separate holdout images

`holdout.zip` contains 12,630 JPEG images in one folder, with no class labels.
Use this separate dataset after choosing the final model with the internal
validation set. It stays out of training and model selection. The numeric
filenames are image identifiers, not class labels.

Apply the same RGB conversion, resizing, and normalization as the training
images. Read directly from the archive in batches, then save one prediction
per image to `cnn_training_output/lighting_enhanced/holdout_predictions.csv`. Each prediction
includes the numbered class folder and its model probability. Probabilities
do not establish whether a prediction is correct.

```{python}
holdout_archive = NOTEBOOK_DIR / "holdout.zip"
with ZipFile(holdout_archive) as archive:
    holdout_members = sorted(
        member.filename for member in archive.infolist()
        if not member.is_dir()
        and PurePosixPath(member.filename).suffix.lower() == ".jpg"
    )
if not holdout_members:
    raise ValueError("No JPEG images found in holdout.zip.")

def read_holdout_images():
    with ZipFile(holdout_archive) as archive:
        for name in holdout_members:
            yield archive.read(name)

holdout_ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_generator(
    read_holdout_images,
    output_signature=tf.TensorSpec(shape=(), dtype=tf.string),
)
holdout_ds = holdout_ds.apply(
    tf.data.experimental.assert_cardinality(len(holdout_members))
)
holdout_ds = holdout_ds.map(
    preprocess_holdout, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE
).batch(BATCH_SIZE).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

# Preserve filename order so every prediction matches the correct image.
holdout_probabilities = predict_with_lighting(
    loaded_model, holdout_ds, loaded_inference_variants,
)
holdout_class_indices = holdout_probabilities.argmax(axis=1)
holdout_luminance = np.concatenate([
    mean_luminance(batch).numpy() for batch in holdout_ds
])
holdout_predictions = pd.DataFrame({
    "filename": [PurePosixPath(name).name for name in holdout_members],
    "predicted_class": [loaded_class_names[index] for index in holdout_class_indices],
    "model_probability": holdout_probabilities.max(axis=1),
    "mean_luminance": holdout_luminance,
    "is_dark": holdout_luminance < DARK_LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD,
})
holdout_csv = OUTPUT_DIR / "holdout_predictions.csv"
holdout_predictions.to_csv(holdout_csv, index=False)
holdout_classes_csv = OUTPUT_DIR / "holdout_classes.csv"
holdout_predictions[["predicted_class"]].astype(int).to_csv(holdout_classes_csv, index=False)
print(f"Saved {len(holdout_predictions):,} predictions to {holdout_csv}")
print(f"Saved class-only predictions without leading zeros to {holdout_classes_csv}")
holdout_predictions.head(10)
```

### Brighten the dark images that were unclear during visual review

Mean luminance flags underexposed images. If the earlier visual review CSV is
available, export brighter PNG previews for its dark, unclear examples. Without
that review file, use the six least-confident dark holdout predictions instead.
The preview CSV includes previous and updated predictions for comparison.

The previews retain the original resolution; the CNN applies the same contrast
procedure to its 32-by-32 inputs. Brightening does not establish a correct label:
blur, glare, or missing details can still make the sign unreadable. Visual review
labels remain separate from the labeled validation/test evaluation above.

```{python}
preview_rows = holdout_predictions[holdout_predictions["is_dark"]].copy()
visual_review_path = BASELINE_DIR / "holdout_predictions_visual_review.csv"
if visual_review_path.is_file():
    reviewed_images = pd.read_csv(visual_review_path)
    unclear_filenames = reviewed_images.loc[
        reviewed_images["visual_review"] == "unclear", "filename"
    ]
    preview_rows = preview_rows[preview_rows["filename"].isin(unclear_filenames)]
else:
    preview_rows = preview_rows.nsmallest(6, "model_probability")
preview_rows = preview_rows.sort_values("model_probability").reset_index(drop=True)

previous_holdout_path = PREVIOUS_MODEL_DIR / "holdout_predictions.csv"
if previous_holdout_path.is_file():
    previous_holdout = pd.read_csv(previous_holdout_path, dtype={"predicted_class": str})
    previous_holdout = previous_holdout[["filename", "predicted_class", "model_probability"]]
    preview_rows = preview_rows.merge(
        previous_holdout.rename(columns={
            "predicted_class": "previous_predicted_class",
            "model_probability": "previous_model_probability",
        }), on="filename", how="left", validate="one_to_one",
    )

preview_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / "brightened_previews"
preview_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
members_by_filename = {PurePosixPath(name).name: name for name in holdout_members}
preview_triplets = []
with ZipFile(holdout_archive) as archive:
    for index, example in preview_rows.iterrows():
        original = tf.io.decode_jpeg(
            archive.read(members_by_filename[example["filename"]]), channels=3,
        )
        original = tf.cast(original, tf.float32) / 255.0
        triplet = (original, tf.image.adjust_gamma(original, 0.5), stretch_contrast(original))
        for suffix, image in zip(("original", "gamma", "contrast"), triplet):
            path = preview_dir / f"{Path(example['filename']).stem}_{suffix}.png"
            pixels = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(image, tf.uint8, saturate=True)
            tf.io.write_file(str(path), tf.io.encode_png(pixels))
        if index < 6:
            preview_triplets.append(triplet)
preview_rows["contrast_preview"] = preview_rows["filename"].map(
    lambda name: f"brightened_previews/{Path(name).stem}_contrast.png"
)
preview_rows.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "dark_unclear_image_comparison.csv", index=False)
print(f"Saved original, gamma, and contrast previews for {len(preview_rows)} dark images.")

if preview_triplets:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(preview_triplets), 3,
                             figsize=(10, 3 * len(preview_triplets)), squeeze=False)
    for row, triplet in enumerate(preview_triplets):
        for column, (title, image) in enumerate(zip(
            ("Original", "Gamma 0.5", "Contrast stretch"), triplet,
        )):
            axes[row, column].imshow(image.numpy())
            axes[row, column].set_title(f"{preview_rows.iloc[row]['filename']}: {title}")
            axes[row, column].axis("off")
    plt.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(OUTPUT_DIR / "dark_image_previews.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()
preview_rows.head(10)
```

## Confidence and prediction review

**Karl, Head of AI:**

We'd like you to actually ride in the car for a test drive, based on automation built on your sign recognition model. What performance would you require before you’d ride in the car?

Based on your initial analysis of the data, your team feels:

a. Only an F1 score of 1.00 on all signs would be appropriate.
b. A recall score of 1.00 for all stop signs.
c. An accuracy of 95% would be good enough.
d. An accuracy of 85% or above for all warning/information signs, and 98% or above for all other prohibition and traffic signs.

The probabilities below are model output scores. Use the labeled evaluation and visual checks to assess prediction errors.

### Inspect sample predictions

These examples allow a visual review; they do not replace scoring against known
labels. To calculate holdout accuracy, per-class recall, or a confusion matrix,
we need a separate answer file mapping each filename to its actual class.
Once available, match that file to predictions by filename before scoring.

```{python}
sample_indices = np.random.default_rng(SEED).choice(
    len(holdout_members), size=min(6, len(holdout_members)), replace=False
)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(11, 7))
with ZipFile(holdout_archive) as archive:
    for axis, index in zip(axes.flat, sample_indices):
        image = preprocess_holdout(archive.read(holdout_members[index]))
        prediction = holdout_predictions.iloc[index]
        axis.imshow(image.numpy())
        axis.set_title(
            f"{prediction['filename']}\n"
            f"Class {prediction['predicted_class']} "
            f"(p={prediction['model_probability']:.2f})"
        )
for axis in axes.flat:
    axis.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Check the two manually reviewed holdout examples

The following labels were supplied during visual review: `01280.jpg` belongs
to class `00002`, and `01307.jpg` belongs to class `00019`. This small check
tracks those specific mistakes after retraining. It is not an estimate of
overall holdout accuracy. Model selection above uses the labeled validation
set; these images are not added to the training set.

```{python}
reviewed_labels = pd.DataFrame({
    "filename": ["01280.jpg", "01307.jpg"],
    "actual_class": ["00002", "00019"],
})
reviewed_results = reviewed_labels.merge(
    holdout_predictions, on="filename", how="left", validate="one_to_one",
)
if reviewed_results["predicted_class"].isna().any():
    raise ValueError("A reviewed image is missing from the holdout predictions.")
reviewed_results["correct"] = (
    reviewed_results["actual_class"] == reviewed_results["predicted_class"]
)
previous_predictions_path = BASELINE_DIR / "holdout_predictions.csv"
if previous_predictions_path.is_file():
    previous_predictions = pd.read_csv(
        previous_predictions_path, dtype={"predicted_class": str},
    )[["filename", "predicted_class"]].rename(
        columns={"predicted_class": "previous_predicted_class"}
    )
    reviewed_results = reviewed_results.merge(
        previous_predictions, on="filename", how="left", validate="one_to_one",
    )
reviewed_results.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "reviewed_holdout_checks.csv", index=False)
print(reviewed_results.to_string(index=False))

members_by_filename = {PurePosixPath(name).name: name for name in holdout_members}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4))
with ZipFile(holdout_archive) as archive:
    for axis, (_, example) in zip(axes, reviewed_results.iterrows()):
        image = preprocess_holdout(archive.read(members_by_filename[example["filename"]]))
        axis.imshow(image.numpy())
        axis.set_title(
            f"{example['filename']}\nActual {example['actual_class']}; "
            f"predicted {example['predicted_class']}"
        )
        axis.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(OUTPUT_DIR / "reviewed_holdout_examples.png", dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

Karl, Head of AI
Obviously you'll be using a convolutional neural network to build your model, but will you be using an existing architecture as a starting point, or do you think it'll be better to design your own?

Based on your initial analysis of the data, your team feels:

a. VGG-16 would be a good architecture to use on this data.
b. ResNet would be a good architecture to use on this data.
